title: QELS Dynamic Light Scattering Detector
description: OPQR has a requirement to obtain an advanced dynamic light scattering detector to enhance characterization capabilities for emerging pharmaceutical products and complex biologics. For a quoter's detector to be deemed acceptable, the following salient characteristics shall be met: QELS Dynamic Light Scattering Detector: Real-time hydrodynamic radius measurement capability that operates inline with Field-Flow Fractionation separation to provide simultaneous size characterization as samples elute from the FFF system. Compatibility with Existing FFF System: Must be fully compatible with and integrate seamlessly into the existing FFF system, including hardware connections, software integration with chromatography software, and synchronized data acquisition with existing MALS detectors. High-Sensitivity Detection: Capable of measuring hydrodynamic radii across a wide dynamic range from approximately 10 nm to 1000 nm to accommodate diverse sample types including proteins, protein aggregates, liposomes, and lipid nanoparticles. Orthogonal Size Validation: Provides diffusion-based size measurements that complement separation-based FFF analysis, enabling validation of particle size distributions and detection of sub-populations or aggregates that may not be fully resolved by separation alone. Data Correlation and Analysis: Integrated software functionality that enables direct correlation between molecular weight data from MALS detection and hydrodynamic size from DLS detection to provide comprehensive analysis of absolute molar mass, root-mean-square radius, and hydrodynamic radius. Data Output: Generates validated, audit-trail-compliant data files suitable for regulatory submissions and scientific publications, with full integration into existing software platform for unified data processing and reporting. Maintenance and Support: Technical support, software updates, preventive maintenance, and alignment with FDA's quality assurance requirements for analytical instrumentation. 3.4 Deliverables Ref Description Quantities Required Due Date 3 Quasi-Elastic Light Scattering Unit for FFF 1 120 days after award 3 Installation, instrument qualification and training 1 120 days after contract award. Detector hardware with all necessary cables, connectors, and mounting hardware for integration with existing FFF system. Software licensing and installation files compatible with current chromatography software version. User manuals, technical specifications, and standard operating procedure templates provided in digital format via download or physical media (CD/DVD). CD, DVD and hard copies of deliverables shall not be required to be returned to the Contractor. Deliverables are delivered to the following address: U.S Food and Drug Administration Center for Drug Evaluation and Research / Office of Pharmaceutical Quality / Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Research Attn: TBD 645 S Newstead Avenue St. Louis, M0 63110 3Schedule: Delivery shall be no later than 120 days after contract award. Vendor is responsible for coordination with FDA staff for installation and integration with existing FFF system. FDA staff will provide access to laboratory space and existing instrumentation for installation activities. 3.6 Maintenance and Technical Support: At minimum the contractor must: Provide support via email, phone, and/or web conference for troubleshooting and technical assistance. Provide on-site installation, integration testing, and performance qualification of the detector with existing FFF-MALS system. Provide on-site training for FDA staff on detector operation, data analysis, method development, and routine maintenance procedures. Inspection and Acceptance Criteria Partial acceptance is made upon delivery of all the parts. Full acceptance is made after completion of Installation and Operational Qualification (IQ/OQ) by the contractor that the system meets all the specifications and requirements. Terms of Use Fixed Term License: FDA shall the ability to purchase a new subscription after the original subscription expires to continue the use of the software and to gain access to technical support and product upgrades. Period of Performance The period of performance is 12 months from the installation date of the system. The delivery of the entire system with accessories as outlined in the SOW should be completed within 120 days of award. Instrument installation and qualification should be completed within 120 days of award. Instrument familiarization and training should be completed on the day of installation. Options None Order Type The order type is firm-fixed-price.

These capabilities include Tactical Predictive Intelligence, which leverages Dataminr�s proprietary 13+ year historical data archive to predict how an event may evolve. It also includes Agentic Corroboration & Context, which deploys a fleet of AI agents to instantly scan over 200,000 distinct public information sources�including social media, IoT sensor data, audio transmissions, and the dark web�providing real-time verification. Furthermore, the Government requires the unique capability to track and analyze anomalous airplane transponder signals (ADS-B Signals). The Dataminr First Alert Advanced platform consumes tens of millions of data points per day from radar, ground, and space-based ADS-B receiving stations worldwide. The platform uses proprietary AI methods�ranging from statistical event modeling to deep learning and machine learning�to detect anomalies in this time-series data, alerting watch-standers to critical national security events such as aircraft diverting from scheduled routes or exhibiting unexpected shifts in altitude or course. At this time, the incumbent contractor and original equipment manufacturer (OEM), Dataminr, Inc., is the only source capable of providing all necessary services. The requirement constitutes a highly specialized upgrade of existing, integrated Government software that relies entirely on proprietary data feeds, closed-source algorithms, and intellectual property owned exclusively by the OEM. Dataminr, Inc. maintains no authorized resellers or distributors. No other commercial vendor has the legal right or technical capability to access the existing Government infrastructure, modify the current software instances, or integrate the proprietary "Advanced" agentic AI modules. Contractors shall furnish all requirements. The delivery schedule is based upon the current construction schedule, which is subject to change. The vendor shall not increase prices for a change in delivery date due to construction delays. The awardees� actual delivery dates will be confirmed by VA upon award. The Contractor shall provide services and support at the locations identified in this Scope of Work. The Government reserves the right to add, remove, or modify locations and facilities as mission requirements evolve across the current and future operational footprint. The Contractor shall accommodate these changes within the scope of the contract without disruption to services. Any adjustments to pricing, schedule, or resources resulting from such changes shall be addressed through the appropriate contractual modification process in accordance with the applicable Changes clause. 2.0 General Requirement All equipment to be supplied under the specifications shall be the newest and the most current model of a standard product of a manufacturer of record. A manufacturer of record is defined as a company whose main occupation is the manufacture for sale of items of equipment and which: a. Maintains a factory production line. b. Maintains a stock of replacement parts for the item. c. Maintains engineering drawings, specifications, operating manuals and maintenance manuals. d. Has published and distributed descriptive literature and equipment specifications on the equipment. Any equipment or service as applicable must be in compliance with the Memorandum dated March 6th, 2025, Subject: Electronic Health Record Modernization Standardization (VIEWS 12862405). Upon award: Field verification must be conducted and coordinated with the POC and Activations PM to ensure locations of utility boxes and all items. Shop drawings must be provided prior to installation. Activations PM will contact contractor in regards to specific delivery and installation dates to coordinate with other services. Requirements: Dental Imaging Software License Expansion - 1 X-Ray Unit, Dental, 3D: CS 9600 - 1 Radiographic Unit, Dental, Wall Mounted, 7 mA - 7 Sensor Kit, Dental Imaging System, Size 1 & Size 2 - 7 Specifications: Dental Imaging Software License Expansion: Software License must be included for 3D imaging machine to have the ability to communicate between the machine and VA computers. X-Ray Unit, Dental, 3D: Brand Name: Carestream CS 9600 The system shall be a Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) imaging system capable of performing 2D panoramic, 3D CBCT, dental, oral surgery, endodontic, orthodontic, and maxillofacial applications. System shall be new, current production model. Imaging Capabilities Must provide: 2D digital panoramic imaging 3D CBCT imaging Field of View (FOV) options ranging from small, focused volumes (~5x5 cm) up to large craniofacial volumes (~16x17 cm or equivalent). High-resolution imaging with voxel sizes as small as 75-150 �m (or better). Adjustable FOV selection to limit patient radiation exposure. Metal artifact reduction (MAR) or equivalent technology. Detector & Image Quality Flat panel digital detector technology. High-contrast resolution suitable for: Implant planning Endodontic diagnosis TMJ evaluation Airway analysis Grayscale depth minimum 14-bit or equivalent. Automatic exposure control or programmable exposure settings. Software & Workflow Manufacturer-provided imaging software included. Software shall support: Implant planning tools Nerve tracing Airway measurement TMJ analysis Endodontic assessment DICOM 3.0 compliant. Integration capability with PACS and third-party practice management systems. 3D rendering and multiplanar reconstruction (MPR). Export capability in STL format for surgical guides. Patient Positioning & Ergonomics Open-face design or patient-friendly configuration. Positioning guides (minimum three planes). Adjustable chin rest, head support, and temple supports. Motorized height adjustment. Accommodates standing and seated (wheelchair accessible) patients. Touchscreen interface mounted on unit. Power: 110-240V, 50/60Hz. Compatible with standard dental operatory electrical infrastructure. Network connectivity via Ethernet Dental Radiographic units The system shall be a wall-mounted intraoral dental X-ray unit with extended reach (long arm configuration) for use in general dentistry, oral surgery, and specialty dental clinics. Imaging Performance High-frequency DC X-ray generator. Constant potential output for consistent image quality. Tube voltage approximately 60-70 kVp. Tube current approximately 7 mA (or equivalent). Exposure time range suitable for digital sensors and phosphor plates. Compatible with: Digital intraoral sensors Traditional film Rectangular collimation capability (preferred) to reduce patient dose. Focal spot size approximately 0.7 mm or smaller. Long Arm Configuration Extended arm reach minimum 81 inches (or equivalent). Double-articulating arm for flexible positioning. Smooth, drift-free positioning. Stable tube head that maintains selected position without sag. Wall-mounted installation with appropriate structural support requirements provided. Long arm shall accommodate large operatories and specialty treatment rooms. Control & Interface Wall-mounted control panel. Programmable exposure presets for: Adult anterior/posterior Pediatric anterior/posterior Digital display for exposure time. Manual exposure adjustment capability. Error codes or diagnostic display. Safety & Radiation Protection Compliance with FDA and NCRP radiation standards. Minimum total filtration equivalent to 2.5 mm aluminum at 70 kVp. Dead-man type exposure switch. Minimum source-to-skin distance compliant with federal standards. Audible and visual exposure indicators. Leakage radiation within regulatory limits. Mechanical & Ergonomic Features Lightweight tube head. 360-degree rotational capability at arm and tube head joints. Smooth, low-resistance movement. Sealed, oil-cooled X-ray tube housing. Easy-to-clean surfaces suitable for clinical infection control. Electrical Requirements Standard 110-120V electrical service. Compatible with standard dental operatory electrical infrastructure. Line voltage regulation to ensure stable output. Sensor Kit, Dental Imaging System, Size 1 & Size 2 The system shall consist of direct digital intraoral radiography sensors, Size 1 and Size 2, compatible with standard intraoral dental X-ray generators. Sensors shall be new, current production models designed for high-resolution diagnostic imaging in general dentistry and specialty dental clinics. Sensor Technology CMOS or equivalent digital sensor technology. True resolution minimum 20 line pairs/mm (or equivalent high-resolution performance). Theoretical resolution up to 24 lp/mm (or equivalent). Pixel size approximately 19-20 �m (or better). Active imaging area optimized for diagnostic accuracy. Must include: Size 1 (Pediatric/Anterior) Active area approximately 20 x 30 mm (or equivalent). Slim profile for patient comfort. Rounded corners for intraoral comfort. Size 2 (Adult/Posterior Standard) Active area approximately 26 x 36 mm (or equivalent). Standard adult posterior imaging size. Ergonomic shape for ease of positioning. Image

title: Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Engine (OKE) and Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Subscription Licensing and Deployment Support
description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Clinical Center (CC), Office of Purchasing and Contracts, intends to award a sole-source firm-fixed-price purchase order to Trilogy Innovations, Inc. for Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Engine (OKE) and Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) software subscriptions and associated deployment support. The requirement includes 40 Core Band subscriptions of Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Engine, Premium, Confirmed Stateside Support (SKU MW01016) and six Physical or Virtual Nodes of Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server with Satellite, Premium (SKU RH00008). The subscriptions include Premium Confirmed Stateside Support and are transferable within NIH's internal infrastructure. In addition to the software subscriptions, Trilogy Innovations will provide up to 20 hours of expert-level engineering services to support the initial deployment and configuration of Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Engine within the NIH environment. Services include installation, initial configuration and system readiness, operationalization of the environment for NIH workloads, identification of technical gaps and requirements necessary to support PAS-X onboarding and production readiness, review of the NIH PAS-X OKE environment architecture, and knowledge transfer and configuration documentation, as required. This acquisition is required to support the NIH Clinical Center's transition from paper-based processes and the unsupported StemLab application to the PAS-X application. The current StemLab application has not been supported by its vendor since June 2022. The Clinical Center must comply with strict manufacturing, documentation, and reporting requirements, including requirements applicable to the manufacture and distribution of human cells, tissues, and cellular and tissue-based products. The Red Hat licenses and deployment support will provide the infrastructure necessary for implementation of PAS-X and support the transition from the existing paper-based environment to electronic recordkeeping. Without this acquisition, the program would continue to operate at risk and may be unable to satisfy applicable federal and state requirements. The Government intends to procure this requirement from Trilogy Innovations, Inc. on a sole-source basis. The program office contacted Red Hat regarding the requirement, and Red Hat directed the program office to Trilogy Innovations as the third-party reseller for this acquisition. Trilogy will provide the Red Hat software subscriptions as a pass-through from Carahsoft Technology Corporation/Red Hat, Inc. and will perform the required deployment support. This contract will be for one year. RESPONSE TO NOTICE This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether conducting a competitive procurement is in the best interest of the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE:Law Manager Software License, Maintenance, and Technical Support Services
description: 1. INTRODUCTION & STATUTORY AUTHORITY The United States Coast Guard (USCG), Headquarters Contract Division 4 (CG-HCA-COCO-41), on behalf of the Office of Legal Policy and Program Development (USCG-LPD), intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis with Mitratech, located in Conshohocken, PA. The proposed contract action is to acquire proprietary software licenses, custom support services, ongoing maintenance, and upgrades for the Law Manager software application. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the statutory authority of: 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 253(c)(1), as implemented by FAR Subpart 6.302-1(a)(2)(iii): "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. 2. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The USCG Office of Legal Policy and Program Development (USCG-LPD) has a continuous, mission-critical requirement to obtain technical support services, maintenance support, software upgrades, and application modifications for the Law Manager software. Law Manager serves as the primary system of record and workload repository for approximately 300+ Coast Guard Legal Program personnel across Coast Guard Headquarters, ten District legal offices, several base legal offices, the Office of Physical Disability Evaluations, and their respective clients. Key System Specifications & Structure The Law Manager system comprises six main notebooks/tabs used for tracking, docketing, and case management across all USCG legal practice areas: Entity: Tracks units and individuals associated with cases (witnesses, counsel, judges, experts, plaintiffs, defendants). Matter: Handles legal assistance files and general legal inquiries. Military Justice: Manages military justice actions (e.g., courts-martial) and calculates the Speedy Trial Clock fields based on charges and calendars. Physical Disability (PDES): Evaluates cases for personnel seeking disability benefits. Regulations: Tracks the drafting, clearance, and review of regulatory documents. Claims/Litigation: Tracks affirmative and defensive claims and litigation for or against the USCG. The software is accessed via both a heavy client-installed application (for bulk data entry and speed) and a secure web application (primarily for reservists and personnel outside the Coast Guard Data Network). Scope of Work & Deliverables The contractor will be responsible for the following core tasks: Ongoing Maintenance & Technical Support: Deliver modified production code, technical documentation, operational procedures, and product updates to ensure zero-error system performance during normal business hours. System Configuration & Custom Modifications: Assist with minor configuration changes (e.g., adding/removing fields, re-labeling existing fields, enhancing functionality as the application-image evolves). Software Upgrades & Security Patches: Provide and assist in the installation of all software upgrades, tool sets, and database environment updates. Testing: Develop Conformance Acceptance Testing (CAT) plans and run verification test scripts with mock data for adding, updating, finding, and deleting records within all system notebooks. Optional Report Writing Tool (Section 2.3.1): Acquire a fully compatible, vendor-supported ad hoc report writing and querying tool. Optional Support Hours (Section 2.3.2): Secure up to 1,000 hours of custom technical support to execute USCG-specific modifications. 3. ESTIMATED VALUE & PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The Government anticipates awarding a Fixed Price contract with an estimated total value of $828,845 covering a one (1) year base period and four (4) consecutive one-year option periods: Base Year Period of Performance Start Date: September 30, 2026 End Date September 29, 2027 Option Year 1 September 30, 2027- September 29, 2028 Option Year 2 September 30, 2028- September 29, 2029 Option Year 3 September 30, 2029- September 29, 2030 Option Year 4 September 30, 2030- September 29, 2031 4. SOLE SOURCE DETERMINATION RATIONALE The Law Manager application is a highly customized, proprietary commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software system. Mitratech is the developer, sole intellectual property owner, and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of Law Manager. The justification for sole-source award to Mitratech is based on the following critical technical factors: Access to Source Code & Engineers: Mitratech has sole access to the software engineers who created Law Manager and is the only entity that can resolve deep-level software bugs or configure the application to integrate smoothly with the Coast Guard's standard operating image. Mitratech personnel possess exclusive access to the proprietary source code for current and future releases. Proprietary Technical Documentation: Mitratech personnel utilize proprietary technical documentation and receive unique, specialized internal training/briefings directly from the Law Manager product development team that are unavailable to any third party. Restricted Licensing Policy: Mitratech does not re-license its maintenance agreements for upgrades. No other vendor in the market owns the rights or data to Thomson Elite�s original source code or Mitratech's proprietary assets. Mission Criticality: This software is vital to daily USCG legal operations. Specifically, attorneys must perform immediate, reliable conflict-of-interest checks within the Law Manager database before consulting with clients. It is also the sole vehicle for workload metrics and resource allocation reporting at Coast Guard Headquarters. Significant Cost & Legacy History: In 1999, the Coast Guard abandoned its efforts to migrate mission-critical applications from legacy CTOS to Windows due to database porting failures. After a rigorous selection process, the USCG selected and deployed Law Manager in 2001. A replacement effort would lead to a massive duplication of costs (including a minimum of $828,845 in support, plus undocumented system engineering, data migration, and extensive staff retraining costs) and severe, unacceptable operational disruptions that are impossible to recover through competition. 5. SUBMISSION OF CAPABILITY STATEMENTS Interested firms who believe they can fully meet the Government's requirement may submit a capability statement. Because Mitratech does not re-license its maintenance agreements or share its proprietary source code, any responding firm must provide clear, undeniable written proof of their legal right, authorized partner status, and independent capability to modify and upgrade the Law Manager application without voiding current licensing, warranties, or security configurations. At a minimum, responses must include: Company Profile: Name, physical address, Point of Contact (POC), UEI number, Cage Code, and business size under NAICS 541519. Authorized Documentation: Written authorization directly from the OEM (Mitratech) confirming the respondent has full access to, and authority to edit, the proprietary source code and technical documentation. Staffing Qualifications: Demonstration of qualified personnel (e.g., Project Manager) available during standard business hours (0800�1600 EST) to meet all SOW requirements. Technical Qualifications: A detailed description of the firm's experience supporting Law Manager platforms within the federal sector. Staffing Capabilities: Evidence of qualified personnel (such as a Project Manager meeting the SOW standard of M-F, 0800-1600 EST availability) capable of managing the transition, Conformance Acceptance Testing (CAT), and custom programming requirements. Capability statements must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist listed below no later than September 14, 2026, 3:00 PM EST.

description: 1. INTRODUCTION & STATUTORY AUTHORITY The United States Coast Guard (USCG), Headquarters Contract Division 4 (CG-HCA-COCO-41), on behalf of the Office of Legal Policy and Program Development (USCG-LPD), intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis with Mitratech, located in Conshohocken, PA. The proposed contract action is to acquire proprietary software licenses, custom support services, ongoing maintenance, and upgrades for the Law Manager software application. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the statutory authority of: 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 253(c)(1), as implemented by FAR Subpart 6.302-1(a)(2)(iii): "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. 2. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The USCG Office of Legal Policy and Program Development (USCG-LPD) has a continuous, mission-critical requirement to obtain technical support services, maintenance support, software upgrades, and application modifications for the Law Manager software. Law Manager serves as the primary system of record and workload repository for approximately 300+ Coast Guard Legal Program personnel across Coast Guard Headquarters, ten District legal offices, several base legal offices, the Office of Physical Disability Evaluations, and their respective clients. Key System Specifications & Structure The Law Manager system comprises six main notebooks/tabs used for tracking, docketing, and case management across all USCG legal practice areas: Entity: Tracks units and individuals associated with cases (witnesses, counsel, judges, experts, plaintiffs, defendants). Matter: Handles legal assistance files and general legal inquiries. Military Justice: Manages military justice actions (e.g., courts-martial) and calculates the Speedy Trial Clock fields based on charges and calendars. Physical Disability (PDES): Evaluates cases for personnel seeking disability benefits. Regulations: Tracks the drafting, clearance, and review of regulatory documents. Claims/Litigation: Tracks affirmative and defensive claims and litigation for or against the USCG. The software is accessed via both a heavy client-installed application (for bulk data entry and speed) and a secure web application (primarily for reservists and personnel outside the Coast Guard Data Network). Scope of Work & Deliverables The contractor will be responsible for the following core tasks: Ongoing Maintenance & Technical Support: Deliver modified production code, technical documentation, operational procedures, and product updates to ensure zero-error system performance during normal business hours. System Configuration & Custom Modifications: Assist with minor configuration changes (e.g., adding/removing fields, re-labeling existing fields, enhancing functionality as the application-image evolves). Software Upgrades & Security Patches: Provide and assist in the installation of all software upgrades, tool sets, and database environment updates. Testing: Develop Conformance Acceptance Testing (CAT) plans and run verification test scripts with mock data for adding, updating, finding, and deleting records within all system notebooks. Optional Report Writing Tool (Section 2.3.1): Acquire a fully compatible, vendor-supported ad hoc report writing and querying tool. Optional Support Hours (Section 2.3.2): Secure up to 1,000 hours of custom technical support to execute USCG-specific modifications. 3. ESTIMATED VALUE & PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The Government anticipates awarding a Fixed Price contract with an estimated total value of $828,845 covering a one (1) year base period and four (4) consecutive one-year option periods: Base Year Period of Performance Start Date: September 30, 2026 End Date September 29, 2027 Option Year 1 September 30, 2027- September 29, 2028 Option Year 2 September 30, 2028- September 29, 2029 Option Year 3 September 30, 2029- September 29, 2030 Option Year 4 September 30, 2030- September 29, 2031 4. SOLE SOURCE DETERMINATION RATIONALE The Law Manager application is a highly customized, proprietary commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software system. Mitratech is the developer, sole intellectual property owner, and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of Law Manager. The justification for sole-source award to Mitratech is based on the following critical technical factors: Access to Source Code & Engineers: Mitratech has sole access to the software engineers who created Law Manager and is the only entity that can resolve deep-level software bugs or configure the application to integrate smoothly with the Coast Guard's standard operating image. Mitratech personnel possess exclusive access to the proprietary source code for current and future releases. Proprietary Technical Documentation: Mitratech personnel utilize proprietary technical documentation and receive unique, specialized internal training/briefings directly from the Law Manager product development team that are unavailable to any third party. Restricted Licensing Policy: Mitratech does not re-license its maintenance agreements for upgrades. No other vendor in the market owns the rights or data to Thomson Elite�s original source code or Mitratech's proprietary assets. Mission Criticality: This software is vital to daily USCG legal operations. Specifically, attorneys must perform immediate, reliable conflict-of-interest checks within the Law Manager database before consulting with clients. It is also the sole vehicle for workload metrics and resource allocation reporting at Coast Guard Headquarters. Significant Cost & Legacy History: In 1999, the Coast Guard abandoned its efforts to migrate mission-critical applications from legacy CTOS to Windows due to database porting failures. After a rigorous selection process, the USCG selected and deployed Law Manager in 2001. A replacement effort would lead to a massive duplication of costs (including a minimum of $828,845 in support, plus undocumented system engineering, data migration, and extensive staff retraining costs) and severe, unacceptable operational disruptions that are impossible to recover through competition. 5. SUBMISSION OF CAPABILITY STATEMENTS Interested firms who believe they can fully meet the Government's requirement may submit a capability statement. Because Mitratech does not re-license its maintenance agreements or share its proprietary source code, any responding firm must provide clear, undeniable written proof of their legal right, authorized partner status, and independent capability to modify and upgrade the Law Manager application without voiding current licensing, warranties, or security configurations. At a minimum, responses must include: Company Profile: Name, physical address, Point of Contact (POC), UEI number, Cage Code, and business size under NAICS 541519. Authorized Documentation: Written authorization directly from the OEM (Mitratech) confirming the respondent has full access to, and authority to edit, the proprietary source code and technical documentation. Staffing Qualifications: Demonstration of qualified personnel (e.g., Project Manager) available during standard business hours (0800�1600 EST) to meet all SOW requirements. Technical Qualifications: A detailed description of the firm's experience supporting Law Manager platforms within the federal sector. Staffing Capabilities: Evidence of qualified personnel (such as a Project Manager meeting the SOW standard of M-F, 0800-1600 EST availability) capable of managing the transition, Conformance Acceptance Testing (CAT), and custom programming requirements. Capability statements must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist listed below no later than September 16, 2026, 3:00 PM EST.

title: RFI - Grissom ARB, IN SABER - SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION OF BASE ENGINEERING REQUIREMENTS
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research, planning, and information-gathering purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10 and FAR 15.201. This is not a Sources Sought synopsis or a Request for Proposal (RFP). No contract will be awarded directly from this posting, and the Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation based on this notice. The 434th Contracting Flight (434 CONF/PK), in coordination with the 434th Civil Engineer Squadron (434 CES) at Grissom Air Reserve Base, is seeking technical feedback from the commercial construction and unit-price estimating software industry. The primary goal of this RFI is to gather industry input on a streamlined, performance-based acquisition structure for a future SABER contract. The Government is particularly interested in receiving feedback on how to structure its pricing database requirements to maximize open competition, eliminate the administrative burden of traditional "mock projects," and prevent post-award "Non-Prepriced Item (NPI) creep." 2.0 PROGRAM DESCRIPTION & ANTICIPATED STRATEGY The Government is planning a Single-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) SABER contract with the following anticipated structure: Estimated Ordering Ceiling: $9,000,000.00 over a five (5) year ordering period. Minimum Contract Guarantee: $2,000.00 (to be obligated at time of basic contract award). Scope of Work: Multi-trade maintenance, repair, minor construction, and renovation projects across real property facilities at Grissom ARB. Core trades include carpentry, roofing, excavation, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, masonry, demolition, concrete, and localized hazardous material abatement. Streamlined Price Evaluation (No Mock Project): To drastically accelerate procurement lead times and eliminate unpaid proposal preparation costs for industry, the Government intends to evaluate price strictly based on competitively bidded coefficients (adjustment factors) applied to pre-disclosed, weighted government workload estimates. The traditional "mock project" estimating phase will be bypassed during source selection. Performance-Based Unit Price Database: To support a "no mock project" model legally and defensibly under FAR Part 16 and Part 36, the contract must rely on a highly comprehensive, pre-priced Unit Price Book (UPB) / Construction Task Catalog (CTC) that is locally researched, standardized, granular, and capable of keeping post-award NPIs under 10% of total task order values. 3.0 SPECIFIC AREAS OF INQUIRY & QUESTIONNAIRE Firms choosing to respond are requested to provide detailed, objective feedback on the following five administrative and technical categories: Section 3.1: Performance-Based Technical Equivalency vs. Database Size The Government wants to ensure the pricing database is comprehensive enough to prevent post-award "NPI creep" without establishing arbitrary restrictions that limit competition. Rather than relying on a raw line-item record count as a proxy for database quality, does your firm support defining technical equivalency based on performance outcomes? Specifically, how should the Government measure a database's ability to minimize NPIs to less than 10% of total task order values? To prove database capability without running a labor-intensive "mock project," would your firm support an automated "Coverage Mapping Report" during source selection? Under this method, the Government would provide a standard, historical list of approximately 100 typical Air Force repair and maintenance tasks. Offerors would run this list against their database to prove they can pre-price 90% or more of the workload value. Detail any software or database limitations to executing this type of coverage report. Describe how your estimating platform and database ensure that unit prices are derived from direct local market research (localized labor, material, equipment, and productivity rates for the Grissom ARB/Indiana area) rather than relying on national averages adjusted by a flat regional index. Section 3.2: Coefficient Absorption & Overhead Definitions To ensure a fair "apples-to-apples" price evaluation, the bidded coefficients must cover all operational overhead. Please confirm your firm's capability to absorb the following overhead costs directly within your proposed bidded coefficients, with no separate or direct billing to the Government: All cost-estimating software licensing, support, and maintenance fees (including providing a minimum of two concurrent user licenses to 434 CES and 434 CONF personnel). Unrestricted on-base office operations, project manager training, and material storage yard maintenance. Maintenance of a localized physical/digital material submittal library. Basic design, drafting, site verification, and as-built drawing preparation. What standard RFP definitions are required in Section L to ensure all offerors are absorbing these exact overhead elements on a common basis? Section 3.3: Safeguards Against Unbalanced Bidding Without a mock project, a primary risk is that a contractor may submit an artificially low standard-hours coefficient to win the award, intending to recover margins through unconstrained Non-Prepriced Items (NPIs) or non-standard hours. Does your firm support a solicitation restriction that locks the NPI coefficient (the markup applied to raw subcontractor quotes) to a factor equal to, or less than, the competitively bidded standard-hours coefficient? What are the industry best practices to prevent unbalanced bidding across auxiliary coefficients (such as secure areas or after-hours work)? Does your firm support capping auxiliary coefficients at a fixed percentage above the standard-hours baseline? What measures does your JOC software platform employ to prevent a contractor from altering unit prices or manipulating quantities after the basic contract is awarded? Section 3.4: Database Update Frequency & Pricing Baselines SABER contracts are subject to severe market and economic price fluctuations over a five-year period. Can your software lock the cost database to a fixed annual baseline for Grissom ARB, adjusting base unit prices once a year via a localized City Cost Index (CCI) update, while keeping bidded coefficients fixed? Does your firm recommend utilizing a separate Economic Price Adjustment (EPA) clause, or do annual localized database updates sufficiently protect both parties from inflation? Section 3.5: Software Cloud Security & Network Access Grissom's local communications squadron maintains strict software security protocols. Is your JOC/SABER estimating software platform a web-based, cloud-accessed system? Does your software platform comply with Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) 2.0 or hold FedRAMP authorization? Provide details of any active Authorities to Operate (ATOs) currently held by your estimating software platform on any active DoD, Air Force, or other federal networks. 4.0 RESPONSE SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Interested firms are requested to submit their RFI Response packages matching the following instructions: Cover Page: Include Company Name, Address, Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email), UEI, CAGE Code, active State of Indiana General Contractor licensing status, and active SBA Socioeconomic Status (e.g., active 8(a) program graduation date). Technical Response: Provide detailed, objective feedback to all items listed in Section 3.0 (Inquiries 3.1 through 3.5). Past Performance: Provide a list of up to three (3) active or completed federal contracts of similar scope and complexity executed within the past five (5) years. For each contract, specify: Contract Number, Agency, and Point of Contact. Pricing mechanism used (e.g., JOC with bidded coefficients, SABER, or traditional lump sum). Total contract value and NPI performance history (demonstrated percentage of work priced out of the pre-priced catalog vs. NPIs). Format & Page Limit: Responses must be in PDF

Handshake holds exclusive intellectual property and proprietary code rights to its multi-school management system, student interface, and candidate engagement architecture. Furthermore, Handshake maintains no authorized third-party resellers, distributors, or channel partners, and sells enterprise software subscriptions directly to federal government entities. title: Chemical Nutrient Analysis Service
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Natick Division, in support of the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC), Soldier Sustainment Directorate (SSD) / Combat Feeding Division (CFD) located in Natick, MA 01760, has a requirement for nutrient analysis services for the U.S. Army Combat Feeding Division. The Combat Feeding Division�s Nutrient Analysis Laboratory (NAL) currently has multiple samples to analyze for nutritional content. The CFD, part of the U.S. Army DEVCOM-SC, is the Department of Defense�s centralized source for all research, development, engineering, and integration of joint service combat rations, food service equipment and field feeding systems. CFD�s primary mission is to ensure Warfighters have the tactical, nutritional and logistical advantage required to survive and win on the battlefield. Although CFD already has an in-house Nutrient Analysis Lab (NAL), there is currently a short-term need to outsource select nutrient analysis services for ingredients and ration components. The contractor shall provide laboratory nutrient analysis testing on provided food samples. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercially available services prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. Request For Proposal (RFP) number is: W911QY-26-R-CHEMICAL-NUTRIENT-ANALYSIS. The Government intends to award a single, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract as a result of this solicitation. All timely offers will be considered, and proposal submission shall be in accordance with Submission Instructions contained herein. Evaluation factors are Technical Capability, Price, and Past Performance. The Government intends to make award to the Offeror whose proposal represents the Best Value to the Government. This requirement is set for full and open competition. This is not set-aside to small businesses. The NAICS code is 541380 - Testing Laboratories and Services. The small business size standard is $19M. The Army�s Office for Small Business Programs concurs with the full and open competition determination. Incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2025-01. FAR Clauses 52.212-1 through 52.212-5 and DFARS 52.212-7001, Contract Terms and Conditions Required to Implement Statutes or Executive Orders Applicable to Defense Acquisitions of Commercial Items (see www.acquisition.gov) apply to this procurement. Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) to be eligible for award. Instructions for registration are available at the website. Any additional contract requirement(s) or terms and conditions determined by the Contracting Officer to be necessary for this acquisition and consistent with customary commercial practices shall apply. Submission Instructions: All Offerors shall submit a proposal consisting of three (3) sections. These three (3) sections shall be labeled; Section I � Technical Proposal; Section II � Pricing Proposal; and Section III � Past Performance. No Pricing Information shall be submitted in Section I. Evaluation will be in accordance with FAR 52.212-2 Evaluation--Commercial Items and Commercial Services. (a) The Government intends to award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to this solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: I. Technical capability of services offered to meet Government requirements: Requirements: The contractor shall be able to analyze samples for the analytes in Table 1 (See Attached Statement of Work for Table 1) with the preferred methods listed below or equivalent* with the listed limits of quantification (LOQ). The main analytes that will be requested are 1) selenium, 2) vitamin B12 (cobalamin) and 3) total dietary fiber. However, the contractor must also have the ability to analyze for any of the other analytes listed below, in case CFD has a need to have those analytes determined as well. This SOW is for an indeterminate quantity of samples (25-100), up to $25K during the period of performance. No more than 25 samples would be sent at one time. Analyses and results shall be completed and delivered to the government no later than 14 calendar days after receipt of samples. Contractor shall prepare a data report for each set of samples that has been analyzed to include sample name/ID, method used, results, units of measure, limit of quantification and date of analysis. *If the contractor proposes to use a different method than the preferred methods listed, than that method must be specified in their proposal as well as the LOQ of that method. If the method is not an industry standard method (publicly available), then please attach a copy of the method in the proposal. During market research the price ranges in Table 2 (See Attached Statement of Work for Table 2) were determined to be reasonable per analyte (dependent on the method proposed). Contractor�s proposals must include the cost/test and the proposed method w/ LOQ. A cost/test can be outside of this range, but the proposals will be evaluated based on the demonstrated ability of the contractor to meet the requirements, proposed methods with LOQ and the cost/test. a. General Requirements In-House Capacity: The contractor must have the in-house capacity (personnel, equipment, etc.) to perform the analyses requested. Contractors acting as pass throughs to larger labs will not be accepted. Accreditation: The contractor shall maintain active ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for the duration of the contract. The accreditation scope must cover the specific nutritional tests requested. Analytical Methodology: All testing must utilize validated, industry-standard methods (e.g., AOAC International, USP, AACC, or equivalent recognized methods). If an alternative method is used, the contractor must provide scientific validation prior to testing. Sample Custody & Tracking: The contractor must maintain a documented chain of custody from sample receipt at the facility until final disposal. Communication & Support: The contractor shall designate a primary point of contact (POC) or project manager to handle inquiries, clarify test results, and resolve sample receipt issues within 24 hours. Storage Conditions: Upon receipt, the contractor shall store all samples under the conditions specified by the government (e.g., ambient, refrigerated at 4�C, or frozen at -20�C) to prevent nutrient degradation before analysis. Sample Retention: The contractor must retain the remaining homogenized sample material for a minimum of 30 calendar days after the final report is delivered, allowing the government to request re-testing if anomalies are found. Disposal: After the 30-day retention period, the contractor shall safely dispose of the food samples in accordance with local environmental regulations at no additional cost to the government. b. Specific Requirements See Attached Statement of Work for Table containing the Specific Requirements and additional details. II. Price: Reference Table 1 & 2 in the attached SOW. III. Past Performance: Offerors are reminded that while the Government may elect to consider data obtained from other sources, the burden of providing thorough and complete past performance information rests with the Offeror. Offerors shall submit three (3) recent and relevant past performance examples performed within the last three years. Each example shall not exceed two (2) pages and shall include the following: 1. description: DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: The U.S. Coast Guard requires services for a contractor to provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, transportation, supervision, and other items and services necessary to remove and replace the existing hydronic boiler, including associated components, control programming and integration, commissioning, and onsite system operating training- located in the McAdams Building at US Coast Guard BASE North Bend. The Government intends to issue a firm fixed price contract for this requirement. The full scope of work and specifications will be included in the solicitation documents. Project Address: U.S. Coast Guard BASE North Bend 2000 Connecticut Ave North Bend, OR 97459 This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 70Z03326QSEAT0120 is issued as a RFQ for removal and replacement of boiler. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The associated NAICS code is 238220 � Plumbing, Heating, and Air Conditioning Contractors This acquisition is set-aside 100% for SMALL BUSINESS. The Size Standard is $19M. A site visit will be held for interested quoters and is highly encouraged. All interested parties must arrive no later than five minutes prior to the start time indicated. Site Visit Date: 09/14/2026 Start Time: 0900 Location: U.S. Coast Guard BASE North Bend 2000 Connecticut Ave North Bend, OR 97459 Please E-mail Ava Stow at ava.m.stow@uscg.mil to RSVP for the site visit no later than 09/11/2026 Any and all questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted in writing to the Contract Specialist at ava.m.stow@uscg.mil with solicitation RFQ number 70Z03326QSEAT0120 in subject line. Questions regarding the statement of work (SOW) will be forwarded to the technical expert for an accurate response. All responses will be uploaded for an equal and fair solicitation to all interested vendors on solely SAM.gov. No more questions will be answered after 09/16/26. All quotes are due by 0800 (PST) 09/21/2026. SUBMISSION OF QUOTES Quotes must be submitted as a single consolidated PDF file electronically to Ava.M.Stow@uscg.mil by the date and time specified in this solicitation. Your quote shall not provide/repeat information already provided in the solicitation such as clauses and provisions. Incomplete submissions that fail to adhere to these instructions may be considered disqualified and ineligible for award. A complete submission shall consist of the following parts: Part 1: Price Quotation A detailed Price Breakdown for the total firm-fixed-price. The breakdown must separate the costs for the following: Direct Labor (Labor categories, hours, and hourly rates) Materials Equipment and Tool Rentals Disposal and Hauling Fees Mobilization Part 2: Technical Proposal The Technical Proposal shall not contain any pricing information. It must provide a clear, concise narrative demonstrating the quoter�s understanding of and ability to meet the requirements of the Statement of Work (SOW). Simply reiterating, paraphrasing, or "parroting" the requirements is not acceptable. The proposal must detail the specific methods, resources, and management techniques the quoter will use to meet the SOW standards. Submit quotes to the following e-mail address by the offer due date and time zone: Attn: Ava Stow E-Mail Address: ava.m.stow@uscg.mil with solicitation RFQ number 70Z03326QSEAT0120 in subject line. Evaluation: The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. An award will be made to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest-priced technically acceptable. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: Technical Capability: The offeror�s proposal will be evaluated to determine if it meets the technical specifications and performance requirements outlined in the SOW. This will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. Past Performance: The Government will evaluate the offeror�s recent references and past performance to assess the risk of contract execution. The Government may utilize CPARS, market research, and references provided by the offeror. Pricing: Price will be evaluated to ensure it is fair and reasonable. Notice of award. A written notice of award or acceptance of an offer furnished to the successful Offeror within the time for acceptance specified in the offer, shall result in a binding contract without further action by either party. Before the offer�s specified expiration time, the Government may accept an offer (or part of an offer), whether or not there are negotiations after its receipt, unless a written notice of withdrawal is received before award. Under FAR 4.1103 prospective contractor shall be registered in System for Award Management (SAM) prior to award. Failure for contractor to be registered in SAM shall result in Contracting Officer proceeding with the next successful registered offeror. Website: www.sam.gov

See the attached Work Item Index for the anticipated ROH requirement. To be eligible for award, the offeror must have an active registration in the System for Awards Management (SAM.gov). Firms with inactive registrations will not be considered for award. Firms must be authorized to do business in the country of performance. Ship repair firms that are interested in applying should submit a capability statement in accordance with the Submission Instructions stated in the below section. The capability statement should include a brief description of your firm and the capabilities to perform a major ship repair overhaul at the shipyard. Highlight relevant work performed that corresponds with the requirements listed in the attached Work Item Index and includes contract types, dollar value of work performed, number of employees, and the number of years your ship repair firm has been in business. Also include your firm�s website address, and, if applicable, experience repairing U.S. Navy ships. Responses should be five (5) pages or less. Please email the capability statement to the Contract Specialist at Kesavan.krishnansingh.ln@us.navy.mil with Capability Statement � Synopsis USS MIGUEL KEITH (ESB-5) ROH. Response in the subject field. All responses are due no later than fifteen (15) calendar days after the issue date of this synopsis notice. Telephone or fax submissions will not be accepted. The Government will only accept electronic submission of interest and capability.

title: M82 and M82A1 Percussion Primers
description: The Army Contracting Command - Rock Island is issuing Request for Proposal, W519TC-25-R-0016, to the SAM.GOV website with a closing date of 31 August 2026. This requirement is for the M82 and M82A1 Percussion Primers: (a) Nomenclature: M82 Percussion Primer NSN: 1390-01-648-3692 DODIC: N523 (b) Nomenclature: M82A1 Percussion Primer NSN: 1390-01-675-6755 DODIC: NA35 The applicable NAICS code is 332993. This acquisition is restricted to the United States, its outlying areas, and Canada in accordance with Public Interest Determination Under Section 3204(a)(7) of Title 10, United States Code and FRO 6.103-7(b). The United States Government (USG) intends to award two (2) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts with five, twelve month ordering periods. However, the USG reserves the right to deviate on the number of contract awards based on the USG's requirements and if determined to be in its best interest. Therefore, the USG may make a single award, three awards, or no award at all. The USG will be using Best Value source selection procedures incorporating Fixed Priced with Economic Price Adjustment pricing. The technical data package (TDP) is classified as Distribution D limited distribution. This TDP contains technical data whose import is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act, (Title 22, U.S.C., Sec 2751 et seq.) or the Export Administration Act of 1979, as amended titled, 50 U.S.C. App 2401 et seq. Violations of these export laws are subject to severe criminal penalties. Disseminate IAW provisions of DoD Directive 5230.25. Offerors must be registered with the U.S./Canada Joint Certification Office to obtain the TDP. The TDP will NOT be available until after the solicitation is formally issued on the SAM.GOV website, with valid contractor credentials. NOTE: This solicitation will be issued electronically as will any amendments thereto. Because of this, the Government is under no obligation and is in fact unable to maintain a bidder's mailing list. title: GEOSPATIAL INTELLIGENCE PROCESSING AND EXPLOITATION (GeoPEX)
description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Geospatial Intelligence Processing and Exploitation (GeoPEX) BAA NUMBER: BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 SEP 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 SEP 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY22 � 30 Sep 2021 FY23 � 30 Sep 2022 FY24 � 30 Sep 2023 FY25 � 30 Sep 2024 FY26 � 30 Sep 2025 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the Beta SAM website at https://beta.SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking white papers for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to provide geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) in all its forms and from whatever source - imagery, imagery intelligence, or geospatial data and information - to ensure a solid foundation of knowledge for planning, decision, and action while creating tailored, customer-specific geospatial intelligence, analytic services, and solutions. This BAA is a follow-on to BAA FA8750-17-S-7004 Knowledge Aided GEOINT Latency Reduction (KAGLR) BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99.9M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 24 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $250K to $10M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Bernard J. Clarke AFRL/RIGD 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)330-2106 Email: Bernard.Clarke@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below: Amber Buckley Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. In the event a security risk is identified and the Government has determined the security risk exceeds the acceptable threshold, the Contractor/Recipient will be notified and informed of the termination/decline of award. After award, the Contractor/Recipient will be required to re-submit the Standard Form 424 as an annual requirement to the points of contact listed above. No other changes are made. description: Marine Atlantic Inc. Request for Proposal #305-379-026 Drydocking & Refit Services for the M.V. Highlanders Marine Atlantic Inc. (“MAI”) invites proposals from suppliers for Drydocking & Refit Services. MAI is looking for a supplier to provide drydocking, refit, inspection, maintenance, repair, and preservation services for the MV Highlanders, including all required shipyard services, labour, facilities, equipment, project coordination, and support necessary to perform the work. Services include vessel inspections, mechanical and electrical maintenance, structural repairs, coating and preservation activities, safety equipment servicing, and associated class and regulatory certification activities. The M.V. Highlanders is available to come out of service for refit during the period April 7, 2027, to May 31, 2027 (the “Available Out of Service Period”). Marine Atlantic reserves the right to accept proposals in whole or in part.  The lowest priced, or any, proposal will not necessarily be accepted.   The closing for receipt of proposals will be 2:00 pm Atlantic Time, September 14, 2026. All documents related to the above noted procurement will only be available through the Merx electronic Bid Submission website. Proposals must be submitted by electronic means using MERX EBS. This will be the only method of response accepted for consideration. Proposals will not be considered if submitted by fax, email or other open forms of communication.   Proposals must be received by the closing date and time.  Late proposals will not be considered. (« MAI ») invite les fournisseurs à soumettre des propositions pour des services de mise en cale sèche et de remise en état. MAI cherche un fournisseur pour fournir des services de mise en cale sèche, de remise en état, d'inspection, d'entretien, de réparation et de préservation pour le MV Highlanders, y compris l'ensemble des services de chantier naval requis, la main-d'œuvre, les installations, les équipements, la coordination du projet et le soutien nécessaire à la réalisation des travaux. Services comprends les inspections du navire, l'entretien mécanique et électrique, les réparations structurelles, les travaux de revêtement et de préservation, l'entretien des équipements de sécurité, ainsi que les démarches associées en matière de certification de classe et de conformité réglementaire. Le M.V. Highlanders est disponible pour être mis hors service en vue d'une remise en état pendant la période comprise entre le 7 avril 2027 et le 31 mai 2027 (la « période de mise hors service »). Marine Atlantique se réserve le droit d’accepter des offres en tout ou en partie. L’offre la plus basse ou toute autre offre ne sera pas nécessairement acceptée.   La date limite de réception des devis est fixée au 14 septembre 2026 à 14 h (heure de l’Atlantique). Tous les documents relatifs à l’appel d’offres susmentionné seront uniquement disponibles sur le site web de soumission électronique des offres MERX. Les propositions doivent être soumises par voie électronique à l’aide du système MERX EBS. Ce sera la seule méthode de soumission acceptée pour examen. Les propositions ne seront pas prises en considération si elles sont soumises par télécopie, courriel ou tout autre moyen de communication non sécurisé. title: 155mm Artillery Cannister Assembly
description: Description Important Information: This market survey is for informational and planning purposes only and shall NOT be construed as a Request for Proposal; therefore, no contract will be awarded from this announcement or any follow-up information requests. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment by the government for any purpose other than market research. Requirement: The United States (U.S.) Army Contracting Command- Rock Island at Picatinny(ACC-RI-Pica) on behalf of the Office of the Project Manager for Combat Ammunition Systems (PM CAS) both located at Picatinny Arsenal, ACC is conducting market research to identify potential sources within the National Technology Industrial Base , capable of manufacturing and delivering the 155mm Artillery Cannister Assembly (hereafter referred to as �Cannister Assembly�). The Cannister Assembly is made from four components: Payload Canister (4140 steel), Payload Cover (7075 T6 aluminum) Clocking Keys 1 Clocking Keys 2 (AISI S2 tool steel or S7 as alternate). The purpose of this market survey is to obtain potential sources in addition to current producers to deliver Cannister Assemblies at a rate of no less than 450 cannisters per year by October 2027, no less than 1,000 cannisters per year by March 2028, and no less than 10,000 canisters per year by January 2031. 1. Payload Canister -The cannister (SK02662) is approximately 17 inches in length and 5 inches in diameter, requires a smooth surface finish free of any burrs, and a protective coating against environmental corrosion. The cannister shall be subject to dimensional quality controls to ensure proper form, fit, and function. The cannister must be produced from a 4140 steel, with a final hardness of 47 HRC. 2. Payload Cover -The cover (SK02663) is approximately 5 inches in length and are designed to cover a quarter of the curvature of the 5 inch diameter cannister. Each cover requires a smooth surface finish free of any burrs, and a protective coating against environmental corrosion. The cannister shall be subject to dimensional quality controls to ensure proper form, fit, and function. The cannister must be produced from a 7075 T6 aluminum. There are no limitations on the manufacturing method to achieve the 7075 T6 properties. 3. Clocking Keys 1- The key 1 (SK02665) is approximately 1 inch in length, 0.5 inches wide, and 0.2 inches in depth. It requires a smooth surface finish free of any burrs, and a protective coating by electrodeposited zinc with supplemental chromate treatment, ASTM B644, classification no. Fe/Zn 12. service condition SC3 (severe), Type I I, color olive drab. The key 1 shall be subject to dimensional quality controls to ensure proper form, fit, and function. Dimensional requirements and tolerances shall apply after plating. The key 1 must be produced from a AISI S2 tool steel or S7 as alternate, with a final hardness of 53 HRC. 4. Clocking Keys 2- The key 2 (SK02666) is approximately 0.5 inch in length, 0.5 inches wide, and 0.2 inches in depth. It requires a smooth surface finish free of any burrs, and a protective coating by electrodeposited zinc with supplemental chromate treatment, ASTM B644, classification no. Fe/Zn 12. service condition SC3 (severe), Type I I, color olive drab. The key 2 shall be subject to dimensional quality controls to ensure proper form, fit, and function. Dimensional requirements and tolerances shall apply after plating. The key 2 must be produced from a AISI S2 tool steel or S7 as alternate, with a final hardness of 53 HRC. All interested sources must be registered in the System for Award Management in order to provide a response. Responses shall include the following information for the Government�s review and assessment: a. Company's contact information including organization�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, business size, taxpayer identification number, Unique Entity ID and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (as applicable); b. A summary that includes a brief description of the contractor's capabilities to include: parent organizations, name/address/point of contact identification/email address, website, potential partnering/teaming arrangements, and manufacturing capabilities to include machining, forging, heat treatment, non-destructive testing, and protective coatings. c. Past manufacturing experience with artillery metal parts, cannister assemblies (155mm) or similar scope(s) of work within the last 10 years; d. A description of facilities/equipment, manufacturing processes, inspection capability, personnel, and Quality Management System certifications or standards used. A description of facilities, equipment including key specifications or capabilities, manufacturing processes, inspection (destructive and non-destructive) capabilities, personnel, past experience as an artillery metal parts producer or a systems contractor, proven monthly production capacity and/or potential capability, and possible partnering/teaming arrangements. Responses should include how the aforementioned factors relate to the specific technical requirements of Cannister Assembly. e. A description of the company's existing production capacity, their projected monthly production, lead times and delivery capability, and their ability to meet the Government's minimum production rate per month. Responses should identify the key pieces of equipment with lead times required to manufacture, test, and inspect product in conformance to the drawings, inclusive of the forging, machining, rotating band welding, heat treating, ultrasonic testing, phosphating, and painting processes. f. Do you offer a commercially available product, or one that can be modified, that would meet the Government�s need for any of these items? Please identify any proprietary information submitted. All information provided will not be returned and will be held in confidential status. The Technical Data Package (TDP) for all metal parts listed above will be made available for informational purposes upon request and receipt of all required documents. Technical data is marked Distribution D; therefore, data distribution is only authorized to the Department of War (DoW) and U.S. DoW contractors. PM CAS reserves the right to deny the release of technical data to any source at its discretion. DoW and U.S. DoW contractors interested in receiving a copy of the TDP are required to submit a signed and completed DD Form 2345, Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement; AMSTA-AR Form 1350, Technical Data Request Questionnaire; and Non-Disclosure Agreement for the Government's consideration. Interested sources shall not reproduce, duplicate, or copy the TDPs, or any portion thereof, except to the extent necessary for, and then only in connection with the preparation and/or submission of a capability statement related to this sources sought notice. This rule applies to distribution of the TDPs to all subcontractors at every level. Upon completion of the purposes for which Government Technical Data has been provided, the contractor is required to destroy all documents, including all reproductions, duplications, or copies thereof as may have been further distributed by the contractor. Destruction of this Technical data shall be accomplished by: shredding, pulping, burning, or melting any physical copies of the TDP and/or deletion or removal of downloaded TDP files from computer drives and electronic devices, and any copies of those files. Within three days after this notice expires, the contractor will notify the point of contact confirming destruction of all Government-provided technical data and certify that no copies were retained. The point of contract for this requirement is Cameron Sacco via email at cameron.h.sacco.civ@army.mil and Christopher Brown via email at christopher.w.brown7.civ@army.mil. All inquiries shall be made via e-mail only. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted.
